result.summary:
WF-03 Step 0.5 registry lookup for ISS-0119. VERDICT: NO PRIOR MATCH. This is NOT a recurrence. Severity stays MAJOR (as filed) -- the Step 0.5 recurrence escalation clause does not fire because no previously-resolved issue describes this root cause.

SEARCH METHOD (grep over docs/issues/*.yaml, 115 files; no file read in bulk). Five symptom-axis greps plus two confirmation passes:
  (A) grep -l "requirement_status" docs/issues/*.yaml -> 10 hits: ISS-0003, 0008, 0009, 0010, 0034, 0037, 0039, 0077, 0109, 0119.
  (B) grep -il "256KB|read tool|read-tool|too large to read|file size limit|outgrown" -> 1 hit: ISS-0119 itself. No other issue in the registry has ever mentioned a read-tool size limit.
  (C) grep -il "append-only|append only|overwrit|schema drift" -> 15 hits: ISS-0021, 0033, 0039, 0041, 0043, 0045, 0063, 0075, 0077, 0079, 0090, 0105, 0106, 0109, 0119.
  (D) grep -il "SCOPE-CHANGE" -> 2 hits: ISS-0039, ISS-0119.
  (E) grep -il "split the file|split by|bound its growth|rotate|archive" -> 6 hits: ISS-0005, 0013, 0014, 0020, 0025, 0119.
  (F) confirmation: grep -iln "REQ-003" docs/issues/*.yaml -> ISS-0119 only. The originating REQ-003 overwrite incident lives in docs/anti-patterns.md, never in the issue registry, so there is no prior issue record of the safeguard itself.
  (G) confirmation: grep -iln "read in full|whole file|context window|token limit" -> ISS-0005, 0018, 0044, 0045, 0051, 0054, 0080, 0119.

PER-CANDIDATE VERDICTS (each title/severity/status header inspected):
  ISS-0003 (MINOR, resolved) -- decision-doc header stale vs REQ-010. Cites requirement_status.yaml only as evidence of a done timestamp. NOT RELATED.
  ISS-0008 (BLOCKER, resolved) -- mix format drift under Elixir 1.20.3. Passing mention of a REQ-013 entry. NOT RELATED.
  ISS-0009 (MINOR, resolved) -- stage-0-foundation.md decision list stale. Passing mention. NOT RELATED.
  ISS-0010 (MINOR, resolved) -- handoffs/registry.json never created. Names requirement_status.yaml only as one of the sources used to reconstruct history. NOT RELATED.
  ISS-0034 (MINOR, resolved) -- stage-2 doc header stale vs REQ-039. Passing mention. NOT RELATED.
  ISS-0037 (MINOR, resolved) -- S4 422 renderer / INV-5 tension. Mentions a `revised` event only. NOT RELATED.
  ISS-0039 (MAJOR, resolved in WF02-REQ042-20260817) -- ADJACENT BUT DISTINCT, and the closest thing in the registry. It is about a Step Final that silently OVERWROTE an already-resolved docs/issues/ISS-0036.yaml with unrelated content. Same failure GENUS (an append/never-rewrite expectation violated, content silently lost) but a different file, a different mechanism (a bad git/file-write in a merge step, not a read that cannot complete), and a different root cause. It also happens to be the one prior issue that mentions SCOPE-CHANGE -- but only as the label of a postscript note it wrote, not as a convention question. MUST NOT BE CONFLATED with ISS-0119.
  ISS-0077 (MAJOR, resolved) -- VariableMerge.merge/3 validation gap. Names requirement_status.yaml only in its affected-files/bookkeeping tail. NOT RELATED.
  ISS-0105 (MINOR, resolved) -- REQ-112 sub-process output-merge schema question. Matched grep (C) on the word "overwrite" in a variable-merge sense. NOT RELATED.
  ISS-0106 (MAJOR, resolved) -- toolchain drift, format/compile failures on main. This is the run (WF03-ISS0106-20260821) whose Step 5b INCIDENTALLY DISCOVERED ISS-0119; it is the parent context, not a prior occurrence of the same defect. NOT A PRIOR MATCH.
  ISS-0109 (MINOR, instrumented) -- tenant-schema-disappears-mid-test failure class. Mentions requirement_status.yaml only to disambiguate its own renumbering. NOT RELATED.
  ISS-0021 / ISS-0033 (MINOR, resolved) -- both about handoffs/registry.json ownership and a stuck BLOCKED entry. Different file, different concern. NOT RELATED.
  ISS-0005 / 0013 / 0014 / 0020 / 0025 -- matched grep (E) only on generic words ("archive", "stale"); all are S0/S1 content questions about tenant modelling, event_retention_policies, Store.archive(), REQ-023 rationale and process_definitions.tenant_id. None proposes splitting or bounding any file. NOT RELATED.
  ISS-0018 / 0044 / 0045 / 0051 / 0054 / 0080 -- matched grep (G) only on incidental phrasing ("grepped the whole file", "read in full" as evidence of diligence, "the whole file's compilation"). None is about a file being too large to read. NOT RELATED.

(a) HAS THIS EXACT ROOT CAUSE BEEN SEEN BEFORE? No. No entry in docs/issues/ has ever recorded that a doc/status file outgrew a tool limit, nor that an instruction became literally unexecutable because of a file's size. Grep (B) returns ISS-0119 alone.

(b) IS THIS A RECURRENCE? No. A recurrence requires a previously-RESOLVED issue whose fix did not hold; no prior issue was ever opened or resolved on this root cause, so there is no earlier fix that could have failed. The WF-03 Step 0.5 rule "if it is recurring, flag severity as at least MAJOR regardless of the original severity" therefore does not apply. Severity remains MAJOR exactly as filed by DOC-UPDATER, on its own merits (a disarmed safeguard protecting an audit trail), not by escalation. Note for the record that the underlying HARM has occurred once before -- ELIXIR-DEV rewriting docs/status/requirement_status.yaml from scratch during REQ-003 -- but that incident is recorded ONLY in docs/anti-patterns.md ("Overwriting docs/status/requirement_status.yaml instead of appending") and was never filed as an ISS record, so it is not a registry recurrence. It is the reason the safeguard exists, which is context for Step 1, not a duplicate.

(c) ADJACENT BUT DISTINCT -- must not be conflated:
  - ISS-0039: silent overwrite of docs/issues/ISS-0036.yaml. Same genus (append expectation violated), different file and different mechanism. Do not merge scope.
  - main's ISS-0111: identity_migration_test's globally destructive bulk DELETE on tenant_schemas. Confirmed by reading its title header: a MAJOR, still-open, entirely unrelated finding. ISS-0119 carries renumbered_from: ISS-0111 purely because of the concurrent-session numbering collision documented in its renumbered_note; the two records share nothing but a retired number.
  - ISS-0118 (MAJOR, open): three runs merged unformatted code past a red format gate. A gate-integrity failure, not a file-size failure. Adjacent only in that both are pipeline-hygiene defects.
  - ISS-0106: parent run, not a prior occurrence.

NO PRIOR ATTEMPT TO SPLIT/BOUND/RESTRUCTURE docs/status/requirement_status.yaml exists anywhere in docs/issues/ (greps A and E), and no prior attempt to fix the append-only safeguard exists (greps C and F). CODE-DESIGNER is designing on green field here, with no superseded prior remedy to account for.

No root-cause diagnosis and no fix are offered in this step (that is Step 1). No file outside this handoff was modified.
